change: Speculative decoding is on in both runtimes, with a different draft in each: mlx-node runs the DeepSeek DSpark draft in 7-token blocks, llama.cpp runs the Google Gemma 4 assistant MTP draft at depth 3, because llama.cpp cannot run the DSpark draft. Inputs, token IDs, model, cases, repetitions, warmup, cooldowns and order are unchanged from v1.

source.wrapper: Pi 0.84.4; reconstructed at measurement time because the historical system prompt was absent. Use the frozen messages; do not regenerate the wrapper.

notes: The DSpark draft (BF16) was trained on the non-QAT gemma-4-12B-it; the target is the QAT Q4_0 GGUF.
The llama.cpp assistant draft is Q4_0, converted by ggml-org from google/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-q4_0-unquantized-assistant.

llama.cpp cannot run the DSpark draft: its converter refuses final_logit_softcapping (conversion/gemma.py), this draft has 30.0, and its DFlash graph softcaps only DFlash2 logits, while DSpark adds its Markov bias to the softcapped logits.

protocol.sampling: Greedy, high thinking. Speculative decoding in both runtimes with different drafts: mlx-node DSpark, 7-token blocks; llama.cpp Gemma 4 assistant MTP, 3 drafted tokens per verify step. Greedy verification in both.

speculation.mlx-node: Gemma4Model.load(target, { draftModelPath: <DSpark directory> }); request enableMtp true, mtpDepth 7, mtpAdaptiveDepth false (pins full blocks; no break-even switch to plain decoding). DSpark verifies on the block-paged cache.
speculation.llama.cpp: -md <assistant GGUF> plus the speculative arguments in llamaServerArgs. The assistant reads the target K/V.

protocol.kvCache: Target K/V BF16 in both runtimes.
protocol.promptCache: Reset before each request; assert zero cached tokens. Adaptive model-local state survives reset.
protocol.timing: Exclude loading and warmup. Native prefill-to-first-token, which in mlx-node includes filling the DSpark draft context from the target hidden states; decode covers the subsequent 255 tokens, drafting and verification included. Record request wall time separately.
protocol.llamaThreadsNote: Six CPU threads records this matrix; record any change when benchmarking another machine, rather than treating it as a universal optimum.

reuse: Keep this version unchanged. New messages, tool definitions, tokenizer, template, drafts or speculative settings require a new fixture version; token IDs are model-specific. Outputs may differ and do not establish quality parity.
